Additional info: I'm in Houston and I'm completely new to gardening
I'm thinking about starting my first garden, but don't know where or how to start. If you can help with any advice I would appreciate it.
What would you like to grow? What size area do you have?
I'm think about a 6x6 area to start off with then expanding, and maybe tomatoes, carrots and potatoes.

Do you have a location in mind that gets full sun? You should not plant tomatoes and potatoes next to eachother, as they are both from the same family of plants (Nightshades.) Subsequently, certain crop diseases can jump with relative ease between both. You should also take the spacing recommendations for each crop into consideration when tilling up your plot.
I don't have a spot yet, but I thought it would be smarter to get help and info before actually starting so I have some clue as to what I'm doing.

I think that you're on the right track. My opinion is that the best piece of advice anyone can give you is this: it's okay to fuck things up. My first garden was planted in a 4' x 14' partially shaded raised bed. I stuffed so much in there that some of my crop yields were puny little things. Hell, I potted and brought my purple pepper into the house so it could fruit rather than freeze. I've found making peace with this to be liberating. Culturally speaking, we're not fantastic a failing in western culture, even if it's an integral part of learning. I guess what I'm trying to get as is that gardening demands that you grow with it. You'll be fine.

Just a warning about buying seeds....there are a LOT of seeds in those little packages! Mistake for many first-time vegetable gardeners, planting too many first time round. There's so much to choose from, and usually 20-50 seeds in a pack. Try to plan carefully using the positioning guidelines on the package, and plant only a few extras for "just in case" redundancy.
